title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: evangelizing mandate does not clash with reprobating will — passover antecedes final hardness, not from foresight of it
pass_a_gloss: Now truly we are commanded to preach the Gospel unto many whom God in this infallible ordination unto grace and glory, from his mere good pleasure, willed to pass by. The mandate of evangelizing therefore does not fight with the will of reprobating. I add also, He willed to pass them by, as to the preparation of this special and in-fact saving grace, by a will preceding their final hardness, and not emanating from foresight of this final hardness and unbelief. For (as has often been said) the final impenitence and unbelief of this or that singular person is not foreseen or preconsidered by God as absolutely and certainly future, except the decree of reprobation concerning the same person being established, by which God decreed not to pity such a person so far as to soften and convert him efficaciously; by which also he decreed to will to permit that by his own vice he repel any grace offered, and remain hardened in heart unto the end of his life.
pass_b_english: We are commanded to preach the Gospel to many whom God, in that infallible ordination to grace and glory, from mere good pleasure willed to pass by. So the evangelizing mandate does not clash with the reprobating will. I add: he willed to pass them by as to preparing this special, actually saving grace — by a will that precedes their final hardness, not one that flows from foresight of that final hardness and unbelief. For (as often said) a particular person's final impenitence and unbelief is not foreseen by God as absolutely certain until the reprobation decree for that person stands — whereby God decreed not to pity them so far as to soften and convert them efficaciously, and also decreed to permit them by their own vice to repel any offered grace and stay hard-hearted to life's end.
source_text: Jam vero jubemur Evangelium multis praedicare, quos Deus in hac infallibili ordinatione ad gratiam et gloriam, ex mero suo beneplacito, voluit praeterire. Mandatum igitur Evangelizandi non pugnat cum voluntate reprobandi. Addo etiam, Praeterire illos voluit, quoad praeparationem specialis hujus gratiae et de facto salutiferae, voluntate duritiam illorum finalem antecedente, et non ex praevisione finalis hujus duritiae et infidelitatis emanante. Nam (ut saepe dictum est) finalis impoenitentia et infidelitas hujus aut illius singularis personae non praevidetur aut praeconsideratur a Deo tanquam absolute et certo futura, nisi decreto reprobationis quoad eandem personam stabilito, quo Deus statuit, nolle talis personae eousque misereri ut efficaciter eam emolliat et convertat; quo etiam statuit, velle permittere ut suo vitio quamlibet gratiam oblatam repellat, et obduratus corde ad finem usque vitae suae permaneat.
